title: First Ctrl+C gracefully shuts down the active spawned command group and exits 130
description:
Implement the first-interrupt shutdown sequence.

## Scope
- Stop scheduling new work on first `SIGINT`
- Wake from active loop work toward shutdown
- If a main child command or `--items-cmd` invocation is running, send `SIGINT` to its process group
- Wait up to `5s`
- If still running, send `SIGTERM` to the process group
- Wait up to `2s`
- If still running, send `SIGKILL` to the process group
- Wait for the immediate child before exiting `130`

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§12, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§9.1, 9.2, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ctrl+C during a running main child exits `130` after the documented graceful process-group shutdown sequence
- Ctrl+C during a running `--items-cmd` exits `130` after the documented graceful process-group shutdown sequence
- No new iterations are scheduled after the first Ctrl+C
notes: Expected to implement and verify first-SIGINT graceful shutdown for both main child and --items-cmd flows, but found prerequisite issue afk-047.4.1 (items-cmd execution path) is still open and afk-047.6.2 (items-cmd timeout supervision) is already in_progress; cannot complete this task's full acceptance criteria without that baseline. Unblocking requires completing afk-047.4.1/.6.2 first or re-scoping acceptance to main-child-only behavior.

title: Second Ctrl+C hard-kills the active spawned command group and exits 130
description:
Implement the hard-stop interrupt path.

## Scope
- Detect a second `SIGINT` during graceful shutdown
- Immediately send `SIGKILL` to the active spawned process group
- Wait up to `500ms` for the immediate child
- Exit `130`

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §12
- `specs/architecture.html` §9.3
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- A second Ctrl+C during graceful shutdown hard-kills the active spawned process group, waits only up to `500ms` for the immediate child, and exits `130`
notes: Blocked: afk-047.6.4 depends on afk-047.6.3 (first SIGINT graceful shutdown), and afk-047.6.3 is currently open with human label due unresolved prerequisite items-cmd supervision work. Cannot implement or verify second-SIGINT hard-kill semantics without the first-SIGINT shutdown path in place.

title: Ctrl+C during empty-batch sleep wakes immediately and exits 130
description:
Implement interruptible sleep behavior.

## Scope
- Make empty-batch sleeps interruptible
- Exit promptly on Ctrl+C without waiting for the full sleep duration

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§8, 12, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §10
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ctrl+C during empty-batch sleep wakes immediately and exits `130`

title: Grandchildren that remain in the spawned process group are cleaned up on timeout and interrupt
description:
Implement the cleanup guarantee for descendant processes that stay in the spawned group.

## Scope
- Signal the spawned process group rather than only the immediate child
- Verify cleanup for descendants that remain in that group
- Preserve the documented best-effort boundary for daemonized escapees

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§10, 12
- `specs/architecture.html` §§9, 9.1
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- Grandchildren that remain in the spawned process group are cleaned up on timeout
- Grandchildren that remain in the spawned process group are cleaned up on interrupt

title: Fail-stop exits on the first non-zero or signaled main child result in fixed-count and daemon non-item work
description:
Implement stop-on-failure behavior for fixed-count and daemon non-item runs.

## Scope
- Stop on the first non-zero main child exit in fixed-count and daemon non-item runs
- Treat signaled main child termination as `128 + signal`
- Return that code as the final exit

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.2, 9, 9.1, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§7, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- Under `--fail stop`, fixed-count work exits with the first non-zero main child result
- Under `--fail stop`, daemon non-item work exits with the first non-zero main child result instead of rerunning
- A signaled main child is surfaced as `128 + signal` and stops the fixed-count or daemon run under `--fail stop`
notes: Implemented fail-stop behavior for non-item loops: fixed-count now returns the first non-zero main-child exit code and stops further attempts; daemon non-item loop now executes back-to-back invocations and under --fail stop exits on first non-zero. Added signal mapping for main-child termination to 128+signal and tests for fixed/daemon fail-stop and signaled exits.

title: Until-success stops on the first zero exit for fixed and daemon non-item runs
description:
Implement the success-until policy for non-item runs.

## Scope
- Stop on the first zero main child exit
- Treat signaled main child termination as `128 + signal` while evaluating retries
- In fixed mode, return the last non-zero code when attempts are exhausted, or `1` if none is available
- In daemon mode, continue until the first zero exit

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§9, 9.1, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§7, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixed `--until-success` exits `0` on the first successful main child run
- If fixed attempts are exhausted without success, `afk` exits with the last non-zero code, or `1` if none is available
- Daemon `--until-success` exits `0` on the first successful main child run
- Signaled main child results are treated as non-zero failures under `--until-success`; fixed mode keeps retrying until success or exhaustion, and daemon mode keeps retrying until success or interrupt
notes: Implemented until-success policy for non-item fixed and daemon loops in internal/afk/loop.go. Fixed mode now exits 0 on first success, tracks last non-zero while retrying, and returns last non-zero (fallback 1) when attempts exhaust. Daemon mode now retries non-zero results (including signaled exits mapped to 128+signal) until first success. Added acceptance tests in internal/afk/main_test.go for fixed early success, fixed exhaustion exit code, daemon early success, and signaled retry behavior in fixed+daemon.

title: Continue and stop behavior apply the same way to static and dynamic item-driven runs
description:
Extend failure behavior from fixed loops to item-driven execution.

## Scope
- Apply continue behavior to static item-driven work
- Apply continue behavior to dynamic item-driven work
- Apply stop behavior to both static and dynamic item-driven work
- Treat signaled main child termination as `128 + signal` before applying continue or stop behavior
- Treat timed-out main child termination as synthetic exit code `124` before applying continue or stop behavior

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.3, 5.4, 9, 9.1, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§5, 7, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- Under default behavior, item-driven work completes the requested item work and exits `0` despite non-zero main child exits
- Under `--fail stop`, static and dynamic item-driven runs stop on the first non-zero main child result and return that code
- In item-driven work, a signaled main child is treated as `128 + signal`; default behavior continues to remaining items, while `--fail stop` returns that code immediately
- In item-driven work, a timed-out main child is treated as synthetic `124`; default behavior continues to remaining items, while `--fail stop` returns `124` immediately

title: Main child timeout result 124 follows the active failure policy
description:
Apply the documented failure-policy behavior to main child timeouts after timeout cleanup has surfaced a synthetic result code.

## Scope
- Treat surfaced main child timeout results as synthetic exit code `124`
- Apply `124` through continue, stop, and until-success decisions
- Cover fixed-count and daemon non-item behavior where those policies apply

## Out of scope
- Main child start failures
- Source-command failures
- Timeout cleanup mechanics for spawned process groups

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§9, 9.1, 10, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§7, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- With `--fail stop`, a timed-out main child exits `124`
- Under default continue behavior, timed-out fixed-count work still completes the remaining attempts and exits `0`
- Under fixed `--until-success`, exhausted attempts exit `124` when the last failure was a timeout

title: Main child timeouts terminate the spawned process group and surface synthetic exit 124
description:
Implement the timeout path for main child invocations.

## Scope
- Apply `--timeout` to each main child process group
- On timeout, send `SIGTERM` to the main child process group
- Wait up to `2s`
- Send `SIGKILL` if the process group is still running
- Wait for the immediate child before proceeding
- Report a synthetic main child result code `124` to later failure-policy handling

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§10, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§8, 9.4, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- A hung main child process group is terminated by the documented timeout cleanup sequence and `afk` waits for the immediate child before proceeding
- After timeout cleanup, the timed-out main child is reported to subsequent decision logic as synthetic result code `124`
notes: Implemented main-child timeout supervision in the non-item loop path: each child now runs in its own process group (Setpgid), timeout sends SIGTERM to the group, waits up to 2s, escalates to SIGKILL if still running, waits for the immediate child, and surfaces synthetic main-child exit 124 for failure-policy handling. Added tests for both TERM-cleanup and SIGKILL-escalation timeout paths.

title: Timed-out items-cmd invocations terminate the spawned process group and exit 1
description:
Implement timeout cleanup for dynamic item-source commands.

## Scope
- Apply `--timeout` to each `--items-cmd` process group
- On timeout, send `SIGTERM` to the `--items-cmd` process group
- Wait up to `2s`
- Send `SIGKILL` if the process group is still running
- Wait for the immediate child before returning
- Discard any captured stdout from the timed-out invocation without parsing items from it
- Exit `1` on `--items-cmd` timeout

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§9.1, 10, 11, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§8, 9.4, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- A hung `--items-cmd` process group is terminated by the documented timeout cleanup sequence
- Timed-out `--items-cmd` invocations discard that invocation's captured stdout, do not parse items from it, and exit `1`

Without that baseline there is no source-command runtime path to apply/verify timeout cleanup and exit-1 behavior. Needs afk-047.4.1 completed first.

title: Empty static item sources skip the main child and exit 0
description:
Implement the zero-item static-source path.

## Scope
- Treat `--items ""` as no items
- Treat whitespace-only newline text as no items
- Treat `--items "[]"` as no items
- Exit `0` without invoking the main child

## Specs

- `specs/architecture.html` §5
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- `--items ""`, whitespace-only newline text, and `--items "[]"` each perform zero main child invocations and exit `0`
notes: Added regression coverage in internal/afk/main_test.go for empty static item sources: --items "", whitespace-only newline text, and --items "[]" all skip main-child execution and return exit 0. Verified via go test ./...; make check is unavailable in this repo (no check target).

title: Non-daemon items-cmd processes the first non-empty batch and exits 0
description:
Implement the first dynamic item-source execution slice.

## Scope
- Execute `--items-cmd` via `/bin/sh -c`
- Capture source stdout for item parsing
- Pass source stderr through unchanged
- Remove inherited `AFK_*` loop-context variables from source env
- Run `--items-cmd` with stdin closed or connected to an empty reader, never inherited from interactive stdin
- Set `AFK_INDEX`, `AFK_ITEM`, `AFK_ITEM_INDEX`, and `AFK_ITEM_COUNT` for main child invocations from the first non-empty batch
- In non-daemon mode, process the first non-empty batch and then exit `0`

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.4, 6, 7, 11, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§5, 8, 12
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 6, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- `afk --items-cmd "printf 'a\nb\n'" -- sh -c 'echo "$AFK_INDEX $AFK_ITEM_INDEX/$AFK_ITEM_COUNT $AFK_ITEM"'` prints `1 0/2 a` then `2 1/2 b` and exits `0`
- `--items-cmd` stdout is captured for parsing and not echoed directly to stdout
- `--items-cmd` stderr is passed through unchanged
- `--items-cmd` does not inherit preexisting `AFK_*` loop-context variables
- `--items-cmd` does not consume inherited parent stdin and behaves as if its stdin were empty
notes: Implemented non-daemon --items-cmd execution path: runs source via /bin/sh -c with AFK_* context removed, captures source stdout for ParseStaticItems, passes source stderr through unchanged, sets item env for main-child invocations from first non-empty batch, and runs source with empty stdin so parent stdin is not consumed. Added behavior tests covering acceptance command output, stdout capture/stderr passthrough, AFK_* stripping, and empty stdin behavior. title: Daemon items-cmd polls again after each exhausted non-empty batch
description:
Extend dynamic item sourcing to recurring daemon polling after work is consumed.

## Scope
- After a non-empty batch is fully processed in daemon mode, invoke `--items-cmd` again
- Preserve batch order within each batch
- Keep `AFK_INDEX` increasing globally across successive batches while `AFK_ITEM_INDEX` and `AFK_ITEM_COUNT` describe the current batch

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.4, 7, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §5
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- In daemon mode, `--items-cmd` is invoked again after the current non-empty batch is exhausted
- Successive non-empty batches are each processed in batch order
- Across successive batches, `AFK_INDEX` continues increasing globally while `AFK_ITEM_INDEX` resets per batch and `AFK_ITEM_COUNT` reflects the current batch size
notes: Implemented daemon --items-cmd repolling after each exhausted non-empty batch. Added TestMainItemsCmdDaemonRepollsAfterExhaustedNonEmptyBatches covering: second poll after first batch, per-batch item ordering, AFK_INDEX global increment across batches, and AFK_ITEM_INDEX/AFK_ITEM_COUNT reset per batch. title: Daemon empty batches sleep for --sleep and then poll again
description:
Implement daemon empty-batch retry behavior.

## Scope
- Detect empty parsed batches in daemon mode
- Sleep for `--sleep`
- Poll `--items-cmd` again after the sleep
- Do not increment `AFK_INDEX` during empty-batch sleep/retry cycles

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.4, 8.1, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §10
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- When daemon `--items-cmd` produces an empty batch, `afk` waits for `--sleep` and then invokes `--items-cmd` again
- Empty-batch sleep/retry cycles in daemon mode do not increment `AFK_INDEX`; it increments only when a main child invocation runs
notes: Implemented daemon empty-batch retry delay: runDaemonDynamicItemLoop now sleeps for cfg.Sleep when --items-cmd returns an empty parsed batch, then polls again without incrementing AFK_INDEX. Added TestMainItemsCmdDaemonSleepsAfterEmptyBatchBeforeRepoll to verify sleep-before-repoll timing, two source polls, and AFK_INDEX staying at 1 for the first main-child invocation after an empty cycle. title: Non-daemon empty batches honor --empty-sleeps and exit immediately when the quota is zero
description:
Implement non-daemon empty-batch retry limits.

## Scope
- Retry empty dynamic batches only while the configured quota remains
- Exit `0` if no non-empty batch is found within the allowed retries
- Exit immediately without sleeping when `--empty-sleeps 0`
- Do not increment `AFK_INDEX` during empty-batch sleep/retry cycles

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.4, 8.2, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §10
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- In non-daemon mode, empty dynamic batches respect `--empty-sleeps`
- With `--empty-sleeps 0`, the first successful empty batch exits `0` without sleeping
- Empty-batch sleep/retry cycles in non-daemon mode do not increment `AFK_INDEX`; it increments only when a main child invocation runs

title: Non-zero items-cmd exits discard captured stdout and exit 1
description:
Implement dynamic source-error behavior.

## Scope
- Treat non-zero `--items-cmd` exits as source errors
- Discard any captured stdout from the failing invocation
- Exit `1` immediately

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.4, 9.1, 11, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§8, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 6, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- A non-zero `--items-cmd` exit discards that invocation's captured stdout, does not parse items from it, and exits `1`

title: Default failure behavior continues fixed-count and daemon non-item work
description:
Implement the default main-child failure behavior for fixed-count and daemon non-item runs.

## Scope
- Use `--fail continue` when no explicit failure policy is set
- Continue after non-zero main child exits in fixed-count and daemon non-item runs
- Treat signaled main child termination as `128 + signal` and continue under the default policy
- In fixed-count mode, exit `0` after all requested attempts complete
- In daemon non-item mode, keep running until interrupted or a documented `afk` error occurs

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.2, 9, 9.1, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§7, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- `afk -n 3 -- sh -c 'exit 7'` attempts three runs and exits `0`
- A signaled main child is treated as `128 + signal`, does not stop fixed-count work under the default policy, and final exit is still `0` after the requested attempts complete
- In daemon mode under the default policy, non-zero or signaled main child results do not stop reruns; `afk` keeps scheduling the next invocation until interrupted or a documented `afk` error occurs

title: Main child start failures exit 127 or 126 immediately and do not retry
description:
Add the documented immediate-exec failure behavior for the main child command.

## Scope
- Detect main child not-found start failures
- Detect cannot-execute start failures
- Exit immediately without further loop attempts
- Bypass loop failure policy

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§9.1, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§8, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- A missing main child command exits `127` with a minimal stderr diagnostic
- A non-executable main child exits `126` with a minimal stderr diagnostic
- Neither case starts additional loop attempts
notes: Implemented immediate main-child start-failure classification: not-found now exits 127 and cannot-execute (EACCES/ENOEXEC) exits 126 with minimal one-line stderr diagnostics. Added tests for both cases asserting immediate exit and no retry behavior even with --loops and --fail continue. title: Daemon mode reruns the non-item main child back-to-back with no built-in delay
description:
Add the non-item daemon driver on top of the direct main-child execution path.

## Scope
- Support `--daemon` for non-item runs
- Re-run the main child continuously
- Do not add built-in delay between successful runs

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §5.2
- `specs/architecture.html` §5
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- In daemon mode, after one successful non-item invocation, `afk` schedules the next invocation immediately with no built-in sleep
- Non-item daemon runs do not add built-in sleep between successful invocations
notes: Added a daemon non-item acceptance test in internal/afk/main_test.go that proves successful iteration 1 immediately schedules iteration 2 (AFK_INDEX output 1 then 2) and exits quickly with --fail stop on the second non-zero exit. This locks in the no built-in delay contract for daemon mode.

title: Parse static newline items with blank-line and CRLF rules
description:
Implement the newline-delimited static item parser contract.

## Scope
- Split on `\n`
- Ignore trailing final newline
- Remove one `\r` before a line-ending `\n`
- Preserve standalone `\r` bytes in non-blank content
- Ignore blank lines defined by trimmed Unicode whitespace

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§6.2, 6.3
- `specs/architecture.html` §7
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§2.3, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- Newline item parsing preserves non-blank line content exactly except for line-ending removal
- CRLF input removes one trailing `\r` before `\n`
- Blank and whitespace-only lines are ignored
notes: Implemented newline parser line-ending handling to match spec 6.2: only lines terminated by LF have one trailing CR removed; standalone CR bytes on a non-LF-terminated final line are preserved. Added unit tests for standalone-CR preservation, CRLF one-CR removal (including double-CR case), and blank Unicode-whitespace line skipping.

title: Parse static JSON-array items and fall back to newline text for non-array JSON
description:
Implement the JSON-array item parser contract.

## Scope
- Parse top-level JSON arrays into items
- Compact non-string JSON values
- Treat empty arrays as no items
- If stdout is valid JSON but not an array, fall back to newline parsing of the original bytes

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§6.1, 6.2, 6.3
- `specs/architecture.html` §7
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§2.3, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- JSON array input produces one item per element
- Object and array items are compact JSON and tests do not rely on object key order
- Valid non-array JSON is parsed as newline-delimited text from the original input
notes: Implemented ParseStaticItems in internal/afk/items.go with JSON-array parsing and newline fallback behavior: top-level arrays are expanded to one item per element, string elements are used as-is, non-string elements are compact JSON via json.Marshal, empty arrays return zero items, and valid non-array JSON falls back to newline parsing of the original input. Added unit tests in internal/afk/items_test.go, including object-item assertions that decode JSON instead of depending on key order.

title: Static item-driven runs process items in source order with AFK_INDEX and AFK_ITEM variables
description:
Run the main child once per parsed static item.

- Execute once per parsed static item
- Preserve source order
- Set `AFK_INDEX`, `AFK_ITEM`, `AFK_ITEM_INDEX`, and `AFK_ITEM_COUNT`

Added behavior test covering expected output for --items $'a\nb'.

title: Fixed-count non-item loops run the main child with AFK_INDEX and passthrough output
description:
Implement the first end-to-end execution slice for non-item loops.

## Scope
- Run the main child directly after `--` without shell-wrapping
- Support `--loops`
- Set `AFK_INDEX` for each invocation
- Remove inherited `AFK_ITEM`, `AFK_ITEM_INDEX`, and `AFK_ITEM_COUNT` from non-item child env
- Inherit parent stdin for each main child invocation
- Pass main child stdout/stderr through unchanged

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.1, 7, 11, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§5, 8, 12
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§2.4, 6, 7, 9

## Acceptance Criteria
- `afk -n 3 -- sh -c 'printf "%s\n" "$AFK_INDEX"'` prints `1`, `2`, `3` and exits `0`
- `afk -n 1 -- printf '%s\n' '$HOME'` prints `$HOME` and exits `0`, proving the main child argv is executed directly without shell expansion
- `printf 'hello\n' | afk -n 1 -- sh -c 'cat'` prints `hello` and exits `0`, proving the main child inherits stdin unchanged
- Main child stdout/stderr are passed through unchanged on their original streams
- Non-item invocations do not inherit stale `AFK_ITEM*` values from the parent environment
notes: Implemented fixed-count non-item main-child execution path: Main now runs loops for explicit --loops, each invocation executes argv directly via os/exec, inherits stdin, passthroughs stdout/stderr unchanged, sets AFK_INDEX, and strips inherited AFK_ITEM/AFK_ITEM_INDEX/AFK_ITEM_COUNT from child env. Added behavior tests in internal/afk/main_test.go covering acceptance criteria.

title: Milestone 6: Process supervision for timeouts and interrupts
description:
Add the process-management guarantees that make `afk` safe for unattended use: per-command timeouts, process groups, interrupt handling, interruptible sleeps, and cleanup/wait semantics.

## Scope
- Start each main child and `--items-cmd` invocation in its own Unix process group
- Apply `--timeout` to each spawned command process group
- On timeout, send `SIGTERM`, wait, then `SIGKILL` if needed
- On first `SIGINT`, stop scheduling new work, wake active sleep, and perform graceful shutdown
- On second `SIGINT`, hard-kill the active process group and exit `130`
- Ensure sleeps are interruptible
- Wait for the immediate child before returning after timeout or interrupt cleanup
- Surface documented timeout and interrupt exits for main child and source-command flows

## Out of scope
- Windows-specific process behavior
- Non-v1 observability or supervisor features

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§10, 12, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§8, 9, 10, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§2.4, 2.8, 5, 7, 9

## Wires up
- Reliable process lifecycle management for spawned command groups and interruptible waits

## Success Criteria
- Child tasks capture the concrete work to implement the documented timeout, interrupt, and process-group cleanup guarantees for unattended v1 execution

title: Milestone 3: Static item parsing and item-driven runs
description:
Add the static item-driven slice of `afk`: parse `--items` according to the documented formats and run the main child once per parsed item with the required loop-context environment.

## Scope
- Parse `--items` as JSON array or newline-delimited text
- Apply CRLF, blank-line, empty-source, and JSON-array rules
- Run once per parsed static item in source order
- Set `AFK_ITEM`, `AFK_ITEM_INDEX`, and `AFK_ITEM_COUNT` for item-driven runs
- Remove inherited item context variables from non-item main child invocations
- Exit `0` with zero invocations for empty static item sources

## Out of scope
- Dynamic `--items-cmd` refresh behavior
- Empty-batch sleep/retry logic
- Timeout and interrupt handling

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.3, 6, 7, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§5, 6, 7
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§2.2, 2.3, 6, 7, 9

## Wires up
- Static item parsing and item-driven main-child environment behavior

## Success Criteria
- Child tasks capture the concrete work to parse static items, respect empty-source behavior, and run item-driven invocations with the documented `AFK_ITEM*` environment contract

title: Milestone 4: Dynamic item-source polling and empty-batch retries
description:
Implement the dynamic item-source flow for `--items-cmd`, including polling, batch refresh, empty-batch sleep/retry behavior, and the documented source IO/environment rules.

## Scope
- Execute `--items-cmd` as `/bin/sh -c` on Unix-like systems
- Capture `--items-cmd` stdout for item parsing and pass its stderr through unchanged
- Reuse the documented item parsing rules for dynamic batches
- In daemon mode, keep polling after each exhausted batch
- In non-daemon mode, process the first non-empty batch and then exit `0`
- Apply `--sleep` and `--empty-sleeps` rules for empty batches
- Treat non-zero `--items-cmd` exit as a source error with exit `1`
- Remove inherited `AFK_*` loop-context variables from `--items-cmd` environment

## Out of scope
- Timeout handling for `--items-cmd`
- User-interrupt and process-group cleanup behavior

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.4, 6, 7, 8, 11, 13, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§5, 8, 10, 12
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§5, 6, 7, 9

## Wires up
- Dynamic item-source polling and empty-batch loop behavior

## Success Criteria
- Child tasks capture the concrete work to poll dynamic item sources, process batches in order, apply empty-batch sleep/retry rules, and enforce the documented `--items-cmd` IO/environment contract

title: Milestone 5: Main child failure behavior and exit-code rules
description:
Implement the v1 rules for what happens after main child failures, successes, signals, and surfaced timeout codes, and how those results determine whether loops continue, stop, or exit.

## Scope
- Implement effective failure-policy selection
- Support `--fail continue`
- Support `--fail stop`
- Support `--until-success`
- Map signaled main child exits to `128 + signal`
- Surface synthetic main child timeout code `124` through failure-policy decisions
- Apply final exit behavior across fixed-count, daemon, and item-driven runs
- Keep main child start failures and source errors outside the main-child failure-policy path

## Out of scope
- Process timeout cleanup mechanics
- Signal delivery and process-group management

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §9
- `specs/architecture.html` §§7, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§2.3, 5, 7, 9

## Wires up
- The behavior that decides whether loops continue or stop after each main child result

## Success Criteria
- Child tasks capture the concrete work to apply the documented failure policies and exit-code rules across the supported loop drivers

title: Milestone 2: Main child execution, fixed loops, and daemon runs
description:
Implement the first end-to-end execution slice of `afk` after CLI parsing: run the main child directly, preserve its output streams, and support non-item loop drivers.

## Scope
- Execute the main child command after `--` directly, not through a shell
- Support fixed-count `--loops`
- Support non-item `--daemon`
- Set `AFK_INDEX` for non-item main child invocations
- Preserve main child stdout/stderr passthrough on original streams
- Handle main child start failures with immediate `126`/`127` exits

## Out of scope
- Static or dynamic item sources
- Timeout and interrupt handling
- Full failure-policy behavior beyond what later milestones cover

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§5.1, 5.2, 7, 9.1, 11, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§5, 8, 12, 13
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§2.1, 2.4, 5, 6, 7, 9

## Wires up
- The first runnable loop path and direct main-child execution contract

## Success Criteria
- Child tasks capture the concrete work to run fixed-count and daemon non-item loops with the documented direct-exec, passthrough, `AFK_INDEX`, and start-failure behavior

title: Milestone 1: CLI skeleton and config validation
description:
Build the first working slice of `afk`: a compilable binary with the v1 CLI shape, config parsing, and usage validation. This establishes the contract the rest of the loop runner will build on.

## Scope

## Out of scope

title: Parse afk CLI args and preserve the child command contract
description:
Implement the v1 CLI parsing rules so `afk` recognizes help early, splits at the first `--`, parses only afk flags before the separator, and preserves the main child command argv exactly as provided.

## Scope
- Recognize `-h` and `--help` before separator validation
- Split args at the first `--`
- Parse only pre-separator args as afk flags
- Preserve all post-separator args unchanged as the main child command
- Track explicit flag usage where validation depends on explicitness

## Out of scope
- Executing the child command
- Evaluating loop behavior

## Specs
- `specs/prd-afk.html` §§4, 13, 15
- `specs/architecture.html` §§5, 7, 8
- `specs/coding-testing-standards.html` §§2.2, 2.3, 7, 9

## Wires up
- Parsed config used by validation and later loop orchestration

## Acceptance
- Help is recognized without requiring `--`
- The first `--` separates afk flags from child argv; later `--` values remain in child argv
- The parser does not rewrite, reorder, or shell-wrap child argv
- Explicit user setting of `--sleep`, `--empty-sleeps`, and `--fail` is distinguishable from defaults
notes: Added internal/afk/config.go ParseArgs with first-separator splitting, pre-separator flag parsing, and raw post-separator CommandArgv preservation. Parse tracks explicit use of --sleep, --empty-sleeps, and --fail via flag.Visit. Added parser tests for separator behavior, help without separator, and explicit-flag tracking defaults vs explicit values.

title: Reject invalid v1 CLI usage with documented exit codes
description:

## Scope
